title: Nobody Gets In After Dark. I Did.
description:
I obtained permission most people never get — after-hours access to Uxmal, one of the most impressive Maya sites in the Yucatan, during a blood moon eclipse.

No tourists. No lights. Just the pyramid, the moon, and questions the official plaques don't answer.

Uxmal has been continuously studied since the 1800s. It still surprises researchers. The alignment of the Pyramid of the Magician to the setting sun on certain dates is precise. The blood moon was not an accident to the Maya — it was a signal.

title: The Door That Shouldn't Exist at Mexico's Oldest Maya Site
description:
15 kilometers north of Merida sits one of the oldest Maya sites in the Yucatan. Over 8,000 identified structures. Most of them have never been excavated.

The most famous feature is the Temple of the Seven Dolls — named for the strange ceramic figures found buried inside its walls. The doorway aligns precisely with the rising sun on the spring and fall equinoxes. The Spanish found this site, built a church directly on top of it, and left the rest untouched.

Most people drive right past it on the way to Chichen Itza.

title: These stones don't match!! INEXPLICABLE NUBS and megaliths at Peru's Pikillaqta
description:
My name is Aaron Hynes, and I've been exploring the world, uncovering the clues that point to a lost, ancient ice age civilization. 
Join me on an exhilarating journey through ancient Peru as I uncover the mysteries of the controversial Sun Gate at Pikillaqta! 🏛️✨

In this episode of Ancient Explorations, I delve deep into the enigmatic ruins of Pikillaqta, a sprawling pre-Inca site built by the Wari civilization over 1,000 years ago. Located just 20 km east of Cusco, this massive archaeological complex spans 50 hectares and features intricate urban planning, adobe walls, and ceremonial structures that baffle historians to this day.

At the heart of the controversy lies the Sun Gate (also known as Rumicolca), an imposing megalithic structure often mistaken for an Inca creation. We'll explore theories suggesting it's far older, with precision stonework that hints at advanced ancient engineering. 

Is it a gateway to the heavens, an aqueduct disguised as a fortress, or evidence of lost technologies? We examine the debates, from Wari abandonment in the 10th century to Inca repurposing, and why some experts question the official timeline.

title: Laser-Cut Granite at the Moon Temple
description:
The Inca didn't carve these. At the Moon Temple outside Cusco, the precision cuts, channels, and nubs in the granite bedrock are a different order of engineering entirely — and the Inca built their walls around whatever was already there.

In this video I explore both sides of the site, climb to the top, document the cuts in the bedrock, the nubs, the megalithic caves, and an incredible mountain relief carved directly into stone.
